headline_marked: [[Starc rips through Bangladesh]] with quick-fire five-wicket haul in Mackay Test
headline: Starc rips through Bangladesh with quick-fire five-wicket haul in Mackay Test
summary: Australia's Mitchell Starc produced a devastating spell, taking five wickets in just 22 deliveries, leaving Bangladesh reeling at 35 for six at lunch on Day 1 of the second Test.
details: Bangladesh endured a nightmare opening session in Mackay, with Australia's pace attack ripping through their top order. Mitchell Starc claimed a quick-fire five-wicket burst, and captain Pat Cummins added to the rout, leaving the Tigers six down at Lunch on Day 1 of the second Test. At the interval, Bangladesh hobbled to 35 for six in 23 overs.

Starc made an immediate impact, needing just one delivery to make the breakthrough by dismissing Shadman Islam for a golden duck. This marked the fourth time the left-arm quick had taken a wicket with the opening delivery of a Test, surpassing West Indies pacer Pedro Collins for this record.

In a devastating spell, Starc continued his assault by removing opener Tanzid Tamim and Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto off successive deliveries in his second over. Both batters departed without scoring, leaving Bangladesh three down with only nine runs on the board.

The left-armer struck again in the fifth over, having Mominul Haque edge one to gully for nine runs. He then dismissed Litton Das for a five-ball duck in his following over, completing his five-wicket haul in just 22 deliveries. This achievement stands as the sixth-fastest five-for in Test history and the 19th of his career.

Starc also moved past England great James Anderson for the most instances of taking a wicket in the first over of a Test, now with nine such dismissals. His previous fastest five-wicket haul was in 15 deliveries against the West Indies in Kingston.

With Starc having inflicted significant damage, Pat Cummins further compounded Bangladesh's misery soon after drinks. In the 16th over, the Australian captain bowled Mushfiqur Rahim for five runs, exposing Bangladesh's tail and leaving Mehidy Hasan Miraz as the last recognised batter.

Bangladesh, currently leading the two-match series 1-0 after their historic nine-wicket victory in Darwin, had arrived in Mackay with the opportunity to secure their first-ever Test series win over Australia. Their previous win was their first Test victory on Australian soil.

Instead of building on their lead, they now face a formidable challenge to stay in the contest following a disastrous opening session. The team will need a significant turnaround to recover from this early setback.

headline: Cabinet Division issues gazette on portfolios for 4 new ministers, 2 state ministers
summary: The gazette, issued late Friday, outlines the responsibilities for the newly sworn-in members, effective immediately. This expands the cabinet's size.
details: The Cabinet Division has issued a gazette notification regarding the distribution and redistribution of responsibilities for four newly sworn-in ministers and two state ministers. This significant announcement was made late on Friday night, outlining the new roles within the government.

The notification, issued under Rule 3 of the Rules of Business, 1996, specifies the portfolios assigned to each individual. The order is set to be effective immediately, marking a swift transition in governmental duties.

Earlier on Friday evening, President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir administered the oath of office to the four full ministers and two state ministers at Bangabhaban. This ceremony formally inducted them into the cabinet.

The newly appointed members include Abdul Moin Khan, Rashiduzzaman Millat, Saching Pru, Andalib Rahman Partha, Humayun Kabir, and Mohammad Shamim Kaysar Linkon. Their specific ministerial roles are now detailed in the gazette.
